title: Voyager 1 Just Reached One Light-Day From Earth — How It Survived 49 Years
description:
On November 18, Voyager 1 reached one light-day from Earth — about 26 billion kilometers. Every command we send takes 24 hours to arrive, and the reply takes another 24 to return.

How did a 1970s spacecraft get this far? How did engineers repair it from billions of kilometers away? And what happens when it finally goes silent? Tell me in the comments: if you were on the team that found the broken memory chip, what would you have done?

title: We Traveled to the Edge of the Universe — and Hit a Wall
description:
We Traveled to the Edge of the Universe — and Hit a Wall

At the very end of the universe, there's a wall. Not even light can get through it. And today, we're going there.

Watch the two counters at the top: how far we've traveled, and how long light from home takes to reach us. They grow from a few kilometers to 46 billion light-years. And tell me in the comments: what's the farthest thing you can see from Earth with the naked eye? You'll find out if you got it right at 11:42.
